reviews.specification:
General operation: assemble and use a lever mass comparator, parameterized by material IDs, support IDs, sample ID, reference ID and mode (assess, assemble, test, compare, inspect, dismantle). Implement the smallest physically supported version: a rigid beam on a stable fulcrum, with a repeatable sample seat on one side and a movable reference on the other. Direct stable seating is sufficient; do not invent cords, pans, machining, calibrated weights or tools. If existing materials cannot retain the loads and pivot repeatably, assessment is a feasible precursor and must report the specific missing physical prerequisites rather than manufacture a working device.
References and integration: reuse and record the item ownership, reach, reservations and transfers underlying pickup and navigate; use existing gather for acquiring material, with its own charges. Reuse probe observation/event infrastructure where applicable, not its name as a substitute for instrument physics. Preserve thin-slice-food-drying-trial equivalence food:thin-slice:air-drying-trial:1 and food-air-exposure-trial equivalence food:whole-unit:air-exposure-trial:1 unchanged. A new comparator does not silently enable their refused instrumentId argument. It can independently compare a reachable sample if moving it is permitted, and any resulting pickup pauses or ends its exposure trial under that trial's existing rules. Candidate inputs include stone item-38-moss-458 and food items item-26-moss-307, item-2-moss-11 and item-48-moss-576, but ownership and current availability must be checked at execution. Do not infer that the absent slice item-48-moss-575 remains available. Observed nearby material sources are not inventory.
Dependencies: deterministic beam geometry, actual load placement, support contact, rigidity, friction/stiction, load retention and structural capacity must exist or be implemented in this handoff before successful construction is executable. Use represented material properties and defensible bounded physical parameters; unknown suitability requires testing, not a guaranteed pass. Compute gravitational torques from actual conserved masses and lever arms, including beam self-weight; resolve pivot resistance and contact failures in code. Physical audit values may drive motion but must never be returned as measured masses or hidden water fractions. Observations expose only visible tilt, displacement, slip, damage and repeatable null ranges. If this mechanism cannot be instantiated from represented material facts, enable only assessment until the missing mechanics or actual materials are supplied. This is not a permanent rejection or era lock.
Costs and work: individual study is 4 simulation rounds at 0.5 energy per round. Development/review waiting costs no simulation time. Assess one reachable candidate assembly or owned material set: 1 round, 0.2 energy, no consumption. Assemble: 3 work rounds at 0.5 energy each, requiring actual beam, fulcrum/support and reference, all within reach and lawfully available. Allocate constituent items to the assembly without duplicating or consuming their mass; reserve only what is actually committed. Each empty or loaded placement/reading costs 1 round and 0.2 energy. A validity test requires at least three independently unloaded/reloaded empty readings and three with the same reference and sample, including approaches from both tilt directions; reference-position adjustments and each subsequent reading use the same per-reading cost. Thus an instrument cannot become validated in a single declarative action. A later before/after comparison requires at least three loaded readings at each endpoint and bracketing empty checks, charged separately. Dismantle: 1 round, 0.2 energy. Travel, gathering and transport remain separate; no fuel is required and no material or reference stock is supplied. Validate reach, energy, permission, item identity, quantity and support suitability before each charged step.
Measurement: use a fixed visibly relocatable sample seat and record its placement uncertainty. Marking or observing positions must use available physical landmarks or an explicitly uncertain visual coordinate along the beam, not an invented ruler. Report a null interval rather than exact balance; include visible-position resolution, opposite-direction hysteresis, reload spread and empty-baseline drift. If intervals do not close, supports slip, loads roll, capacity is exceeded or the beam changes shape, mark the reading invalid. With stable reference mass R, sample arm L, loaded reference position x and empty position x0, the ideal relation is m/R=(x-x0)/L. Return only intervals propagated through observed position uncertainty and bounded friction/geometry errors, never hidden exact m or R. Report resolution in fractions of this particular reference or a supported before/after ratio; kilograms or grams require a separately justified calibrated reference. State that empirical repeatability does not establish absolute accuracy. Do not print an uncertainty narrower than the mechanism and observation model support. If error bounds cannot be justified, report directional comparison only when its torque margin exceeds all represented uncertainties, otherwise inconclusive.
For exposure comparisons, retain exact device, beam, reference and sample IDs; endpoint event IDs and times; setup version; sample placement; null observations; empty checks; and uncertainty method. Confirm the reference and beam stayed intact and sufficiently stable through accessible inspections; weather, wetness, damage or uncertain drift invalidate the assumed equivalence unless bounded. Match the same sample and account for any actually observed additions, removals or residues. A reading made now cannot reconstruct the sample's pre-exposure mass at tick 48 or infer a mass change from earlier shrinkage. Start a new baseline if necessary. A supported decrease establishes net mass change only, not water loss, contamination, nutrient preservation, food safety or causal superiority over a control.
Conservation and ongoing effects: every placed load leaves its former location exactly once and remains an identifiable real item at the apparatus; removal reverses that transfer. Assembly mass is the sum of its components, with no extra inventory weight or fictitious reference units. Non-destructive comparison consumes no food and does not reset age, decay, water, nutrition or toxicity. Existing weather, food decay and exposure rules continue during study, work, use and pauses. Any modeled slip, spill, breakage or residue must persist with conserved material accounting; do not invent detached pieces without a supporting mechanism. No unattended measurements are produced. Maintenance consists of paid empty/reload checks after movement, impacts, visible wetting or configuration changes; repair requires actual materials and supported operations, otherwise dismantle or invalidate.
Lifecycle: persist completed assembly work and observations after every paid step. Interruption stops work immediately; resume revalidates materials and placement, repeating invalidated checks at their normal cost. Cancellation releases reservations and leaves committed materials or the partial assembly physically where they are; dismantling recovers only actually recoverable constituents. Death cancels active work and personal reservations, leaves the apparatus and loads in the world under existing ownership rules, and grants nobody knowledge or permission. Used time and energy are never refunded; unstarted invalid steps are uncharged. Successful assembly, validated comparison, inconclusive result and physical failure are separate observable events. All rules execute in code without recurring model approval; no protected reward accounts, budgets, goals or permissions are modified.
